subject: Performance SLO follow-up: latency targets & cost levers (Nova Retail)
msg_1_subject: Performance SLO follow-up: latency targets & throughput
msg_1_body:
Thanks again for the call earlier, Alex — good to meet the Nova Retail team. Quick recap from our side and next steps so we're aligned:

Recap:
- Primary SLOs discussed: 200ms p95 for search relevance calls (avg prompt ~80 tokens), 150ms p95 for lightweight reranking, and streaming chat responses with first-token under 120ms and follow-on tokens at ~20ms/token if possible.
- Target concurrency/throughput: sustained 800 qps during peak daypart, bursts to 3k qps for short windows.
- Important constraints: sensitive PII redaction, on-prem VPC option may be required for certain stores.

Cost/perf levers we mentioned (high level):
- Continuous batching (lower per-token cost but watch tail latency)
- Prefix/KV caching for repeated context (catalog lookups, user history)
- Quantization profiles (8-bit, 4-bit mixed where quality allows)
- Model variants: lower-latency 7B option for quick responses vs 30-40B for high-quality generation

Asks / next steps:
1) Can you confirm the p95 targets above and the expected average prompt + response length (tokens)?
2) Please share a small sample of representative queries (anonymized) so we can run a dry perf run — attaching our sample format.
3) We’ll do an internal perf/throughput assessment (Priyom + Rishi) and propose concrete batching/cache/quant settings.
4) Quick follow-up: 30-min technical sync next week to review perf run results.

Thanks — I’ll loop in Rishi and Priyom on timing.

—

msg_2_body:
Thanks Marissa — that summary looks right. A couple of clarifications from our side:

- Streaming: yes, we need streaming for the customer chat widget. First-token latency is most critical; after that we can accept slightly higher per-token times as long as the stream maintains rhythm.
- Typical payload sizes: average prompt 70–100 tokens, average response 150–250 tokens. Peak spikes could have longer responses (up to ~600 tokens) for complex product descriptions.
- Concurrency: our initial goal is 800 sustained qps but we need to support bursts to 3k for promotions.

I've attached a small anonymized set of queries (nova_query_samples.jsonl) and our internal latency targets spreadsheet.

Questions for Rishi/Priyom:
- What batching window would you recommend given the streaming requirement?
- Can you estimate the perf delta between 8-bit and 4-bit quant profiles for the 30–40B class?

msg_3_subject: Re: Performance SLO follow-up: latency targets & throughput
msg_3_body:
Hi Alex / Marissa — quick technical notes after scanning the samples. High level answers first, then recommended next steps.

High-level guidance:
- Continuous batching: We recommend an adaptive batching window target of ~5–10ms for streaming-first workloads. That gives meaningful batching benefits while keeping first-token tail latency low. For non-streaming bulk inference (reranks, batch transforms), larger windows (20–50ms) are fine.

- Caching: Prefix/KV caching will be very effective for Nova Retail if you have repeated product/context tokens (catalog IDs, user history). We typically see 20–40% effective token savings on catalog-heavy workloads after warm cache.

- Quantization profiles: For 30–40B models on Ampere/GA100 hardware, 8-bit integer quantization is a conservative default and generally yields ~1.4–1.8x throughput improvement with minimal quality drift for classification/reranking tasks. 4-bit (QLoRA / group-wise) can provide 2–3x throughput but requires careful evals for generation quality on long-form responses. We can run side-by-side evals on your samples.

- Model variants & routing: Use a smaller low-latency model (7B quant) for immediate UI responses and route longer/high-quality generations to the 30–40B profile asynchronously or as a background enrichment. Redwood's routing rules can do A/B or fallback routing by latency budget.

- Autoscaling and warm pools: Maintain a small warm pool to avoid cold-start tails for predictable traffic patterns (promotions). For bursts, we recommend immediate scale up with a short-term burst pool and graceful degradation to a lower-cost variant if capacity constrained.

Suggested perf bench plan (what we can run):
1) Dry-run with your sample file at 100 concurrent to validate correctness and measure baseline p95.
2) Warm cache run (same concurrency) to measure effective token savings.
3) Streaming run with adaptive 5ms window to measure first-token p95 and per-token pacing.
4) Quant profiles: run 8-bit vs 4-bit on representative requests for generation quality + perf delta.

Preliminary estimates (very rough):
- 8-bit quant on 30B -> ~1.5x throughput, small quality hit for long-form;
- 4-bit quant on 30B -> ~2.5x throughput, potential quality degradation on 600-token responses (needs eval);
- 7B 8-bit -> ~3–4x lower latency per request vs 30B, good for short responses.

Action items I can own this week:
- Run baseline dry perf with your attached samples (need confirmation that samples are representative).
- Share a short report with recommended batching window, cache config, and quant profile candidates.

If Tue 3/16 or Wed 3/17 works for a 30-min sync, we can walk through the perf results and proposed config.

—
Rishi Malhotra
Staff SWE, Model Serving, Redwood Inference
